subject: SCIENCE
title: Living or Nonliving?
objective: Use multiple characteristics as evidence when discussing living things.
introduction: A seed can rest for a long time and still be alive. How can you tell if something is living or non-living?

vocabulary.definition: The power to do work, like light or heat.
How a living thing is born, grows, and changes.
A living thing that grows in soil and makes food.

items.prompt: Which statement about living things is true?

options.text: Living things use energy, grow, respond to their surroundings, and belong to life cycles; one visible sign alone is not enough.

items.explanation: Living things grow, use energy, respond, and have life cycles. Movement alone is not proof — a car moves but is not alive, and not every living thing reproduces visibly.

items.prompt: Which statement about living things is correct?

options.text: seed can be dormant and living
a moving toy car is alive

items.explanation: A seed can rest for a long time and still be alive. Fire and toy cars move, but they are not alive.

options.text: fire moves but is not an organism
seed can be dormant and living

items.explanation: Movement alone does not prove life — fire moves but is not alive. A seed can rest and still be alive.

options.text: Movement alone does not prove something is living.

items.explanation: Cars and fire move too, but they are not alive. Living things grow, use energy, and respond to their surroundings.

items.prompt: Which statement about living things is true?
items.explanation: A plant grows and uses energy, which are signs of life. Dormant seeds are still alive, and movement alone does not prove life.
